title: Company-wide policies and process documentation
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This page centralizes Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. Use this document as the canonical reference for process flows, ownership, approval thresholds, and links to role-specific guides.

Purpose and scope
- Purpose: ensure consistent, auditable, and secure decision-making across the company and reduce operational risk.
- Scope: applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party vendors that access company systems or data. Individual teams may publish more detailed procedures that conform to these standards.

1) Access & Permissions
Intro: Access control follows the principle of least privilege with role-based access control (RBAC), centralized SSO, and documented approval flows. All access changes must be auditable.

Key components:
- Identity provider: Okta (SSO + SCIM) is the canonical identity provider.
- Role model: use team-based Roles (e.g., infra-eng, model-onboarding, finance-analyst) mapped to groups in Okta.
- Approval flow: direct manager -> team owner -> IAM admin for sensitive roles.
- Sensitive access: any request granting access to production clusters, customer data, or KMS/HSM keys requires Security review.

Procedure to request access:
1. Submit a request via the Access Request template (link: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/access-request).
2. Manager verifies justification and duration (default: temporary access expires after 30 days).
3. Team owner approves in the request ticketing system (Jira).
4. IAM admin applies group changes via SCIM and records the change ID in the ticket.

Temporary and emergency access:
- Temporary elevated access: maximum 30 days. Extensions require re-approval.
- Emergency access (break-glass): Request via the incident channel and notify Security within 24 hours. All break-glass actions must be backfilled with a formal access ticket and post-incident review.

Ownership and SLAs:
- Owner: IT & Security (it-security@redwood.com).
- SLA: Access requests completed within 72 business hours for standard requests, 4 hours for high-priority security requests.

2) Change Management
Intro: Changes to production services, infra, and customer-facing configs must follow a change control process to minimize risk and provide traceability.

Change categories and approval matrix (table):
- Low-risk (documentation, non-prod config): approver = team owner; timeframe = rolling deployments allowed.
- Medium-risk (infra config, non-customer impacting code): approver = team owner + platform lead; timeframe = scheduled within maintenance window.
- High-risk (database schema changes, customer-facing config, capacity changes): approver = engineering manager + SRE + Security; requires change request and rollout plan.

Standard change procedure:
1. Create a Change Request (CR) in Jira using the Change Request template. Include rollback plan, impact analysis, and testing signoffs.
2. Schedule in the change calendar and notify stakeholders (72h notice recommended for medium/high risk).
3. Execute during the agreed window. Monitor metrics and rollback if SLO degradation occurs.
4. Complete a post-change review within 5 business days and update the CR with findings.

Emergency changes:
- Follow the Emergency Change path: emergency CR is created by the oncall, notified to change-approvers, and retroactively documented within 24 hours. Postmortem required for any emergency change that caused customer impact.

3) Data Management
Intro: Data is classified, stored, and retained according to its sensitivity. Controls and retention ensure compliance with legal and contractual obligations.

Classification levels:
- Public: information approved for public release.
- Internal: default for operational data and internal communications.
- Restricted: PII, customer-provided data, model training inputs that include customer data.
- Regulated: data subject to specific legal/regulatory safeguards.

Storage & encryption:
- All Restricted/Regulated data must be stored in approved regions, encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). Key management integrated with KMS.
- Backups: must be encrypted and tested quarterly for restore.

Retention & deletion:
- Default retention: Internal = 2 years, Restricted = 7 years or customer contract term (whichever is longer), Regulated per legal requirements.
- Data deletion requests: follow Data Subject Request template and route to Data Privacy & Legal.

Access & monitoring:
- Data access requires documented business justification and least-privilege access.
- Audit logs retained for 1 year for standard logs, 7 years for access to Restricted/Regulated data.

Ownership:
- Data steward: product or data owner designated per dataset. Security owns infrastructure controls (it-security@redwood.com).

4) Procurement & Expenses
Intro: Procurement follows an approval and documentation workflow to control spend, comply with contracts, and ensure vendor due diligence.

Approval thresholds (table):
- <= $2,500: individual contributor approval + expense entry.
- $2,501–$25,000: manager approval + procurement request.
- > $25,000: procurement team + finance + legal review.

Procurement steps:
1. Fill Procurement Request template and attach vendor quote.
2. Procurement team validates supplier info, checks vendor risk score, and routes for necessary approvals.
3. Finance opens purchase order (PO) and routes to legal if contract required.
4. Invoice processing: submit invoices to AP with PO number.

Expense policy highlights:
- Use company card where possible. Receipts required for all expenses > $25. Travel per travel policy below.
- Reimbursements: submit within 60 days via the Expenses template (link: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/expense-report).

5) Vendor Management
Intro: Vendors are classified by risk and must pass onboarding checks before production access.

Onboarding checklist:
- Vendor questionnaire completed (security, data handling, SOC reports if available).
- Legal executes contract with appropriate DPAs and indemnity clauses.
- Finance adds vendor to AP system.
- Access provisioning limited to approved service accounts and time-bound keys.

Vendor risk levels and controls:
- Low risk: marketing tools, minor SaaS. Basic contract and PO required.
- Medium risk: vendors handling internal data. Require DPA and security questionnaire.
- High risk: vendors with access to customer data or production systems. Require SOC2/ISO attestation or equivalent, security review, and technical onboarding plan.

Ongoing vendor monitoring:
- Annual review for medium/high risk vendors. Triggered re-assessment on significant vendor changes.

6) Travel Policy
Intro: Travel supports business needs while ensuring cost control and employee safety.

Booking and approvals:
- All travel must be booked through the corporate travel tool or approved by manager. International travel requires travel approval form and security check-in.
- Economy class for flights <= 8 hours; premium economy or business requires manager and finance approval.

Per diem and reimbursement:
- Per diem: continental US = $75/day; international = consult regional table in the Travel template.
- Ground transportation: use rideshare or rental cars following company guidelines. Receipts required for rides >= $25.

Health & safety:
- Register travel with Security when traveling to high-risk regions. Emergency contact: travel-safety@redwood.com.

7) Internal Templates & Links
- Access Request: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/access-request
- Change Request: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/change-request
- Procurement Request: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/procurement-request
- Expense Report: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/expense-report
- Data Subject Request: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/data-subject-request

Governance, exceptions and reviews
- Exceptions: all exceptions to policy require a documented risk assessment and approval by the owner team and Security. Log exceptions in the Risk & Exceptions tracker.
- Reviews: core policies reviewed annually or after any major incident.

Contacts and escalation
- IT & Security: it-security@redwood.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- Finance & AP: finance-ap@redwood.com
- Travel & Safety: travel-safety@redwood.com
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com

Appendix: Quick approval matrix (CSV-friendly)
- Access request: Manager -> Team Owner -> IAM Admin
- Changes: Team Owner -> Platform/SRE -> Security (for high risk)
- Procurement: Manager -> Procurement -> Finance -> Legal (if > $25k)
